content: So, over the last month of so, I have had to learn some standard tactics and proofs used in Algebraic Geometry and Category Theory - and, I don't think I did it in the most efficient way. Maybe, I should have asked this question sooner, but better late than never. How do people go about learning the standard notations, the fundamental lemmas and theorems, specific tactics, etc., in an area of mathematics that you haven't explored before (not explored in mathlib of course - not in general)?

I keep lists of the main definitions/notations, which I find either by browsing open PRs to review or by stumbling onto them being used in nearby lemmas when proving things. I find it helps to take stock and see what we have to work with. There's also the mathlib-phrasebook which could become a similar resource.

For theorems I think Loogle is great; I don't feel the need to get to know lemmas/theorems since I find them when I need them.

For tactics I think reading other people's proofs / reviewing PRs / getting PR reviews work great, although I think for most areas there aren't a lot of area-specific-tactics. (idk about the areas you mentioned but category theory might be special in this regard, e.g. I know it has some fancy attributes to autogenerate stuff)
@Snir Broshi these are kinda cool! I haven't seen them before! Thanks.

I did projects, got stuck, asked questions, made mathlib PRs and got feedback, and talked to people locally (it was slightly surprising to me that I was a professor here but within a few months of teaching lean to the undergraduates there were some who knew parts of the library much better than me! But I was very pleased about this!)
For some areas, there's also deeper documentation (on e.g. the design trade-offs), such as in the form of a published paper or a library note. But not all areas have such papers about them.

My problem with all these papers is that they assume the reader to know math notation. I'd rather have papers (or, even better, textbooks) that explain various mathematical topics using English and Lean only.
